claims.text: The HVAF-i7 feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl with a 15–45 μm particle-size distribution.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition with 15–45 μm feedstock produces acceptable-quality coatings but insufficient thickness.
Modifying the HVAF-i7 nozzle geometry will increase in-flight particle velocity.
The modified nozzle should be operated at spray distances of 300–350 mm.
The process should use standard HVAF-i7 pressures and temperatures.
The intervention will remain effective on internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Increasing particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy and impact momentum.
Particles that are sufficiently molten and have enough velocity form well-flattened splats.
Increasing particle velocity promotes more efficient in-flight melting.
Improved particle state and impact behavior reduce particle rebound.
The nozzle modification will reduce overspray loss.
Reduced rebound and overspray will increase deposited mass and coating thickness.
The modified process will produce a significantly thicker coating than the standard 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline.
The resulting coating will remain well adhered to the substrate.
The modified process will retain oxidation levels comparable to the baseline.
The modified coating will maintain durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The magnitude of the deposition-efficiency and thickness improvement may vary and requires experimental calibration.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thickness increase while preserving oxidation, adhesion, and uniformity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Requiring a 300–350 mm spray distance while depositing within a 120 mm internal diameter is geometrically incompatible with ordinary radial internal-diameter spraying, whose available radial standoff is at most about 60 mm. No alternative axial or angled arrangement is specified.
